rationale: In classical distal hereditary motor neuropathy type 11 (dHMN11 / OMIM #620528) associated with SPTAN1 variants, clinical and electrophysiological presentation is restricted to lower motor neuron involvement without prominent objective sensory loss. Normal sensory nerve action potentials (SNAPs) and sensory conduction velocities distinguish dHMN from axonal Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease (CMT2), which inherently involves significant sensory neuropathy. However, recent literature indicates overlapping spectra across inherited peripheral neuropathies, myopathies, and complex phenotypes caused by SPTAN1 variants.

evidence.text: dHMN caused by pathogenic heterozygous variants in SPTAN1 exhibits normal sensory nerve conduction velocities and normal sensory nerve action potentials, supporting the absence of objective sensory impairment in dHMN.

new_directions.rationale: While SNAPs are normal by definition in dHMN, minor small-fiber sensory involvement could challenge the strict motor-exclusive classification.

new_directions.question_text: Do specific missense versus truncating/nonsense variants in SPTAN1 determine whether a patient manifests pure dHMN versus a broader neuromuscular or myopathic phenotype?
new_directions.rationale: Loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 have been reported in dHMN and distal myopathy, whereas dominant-negative in-frame variants cause severe infantile epileptic encephalopathy.
